0.msg: I welcome you, young one. You are here to learn one of Mu Lung's treasured traditional games?

2.msg: There are many ancient and honorable games played in Mu Lung. Of them, poetry recitation is the most beautiful and elegant.

3.msg: #bWhere I come from, memorizing poems is NOT a game.#k

4.msg: It is indeed a game! Reciting a poem while immersed in nature... There is no greater feeling!

5.msg: #bOh my god, are you secretly a literature professor?#k

6.msg: If only! Now, allow me to demonstrate...

7.msg:
The panda stands\r\n
Holding a book\r\n
Lonely but not alone.\r\n
I should eat myself.\r\n
- Anonymous (certainly not a panda with a jaunty blue hat and elegant beard named Do Gong)

8.msg: Can you feel the overpowering emotion surging through you at those grand lines? Now it is your turn to recite a poem written by a great poet.

9.msg: #bUh, can you just teach me a different game?#k

10.msg: Very well. There is another game as ancient and honorable as poetry battles. It is called... Omok. \r\n#e#b<Maple Omok>#n#k\r Players: 2\r Limit: Up to 10 times a day\r Required Level: Lv. 33+\r Victory Requirements: Connect 5 Omok pieces in a row and you win.\r Reward: #i4001833# #t4001833#

no.0: Tsk, the young do not understand the joy of simple games.

yes.0: It seems a simple game, but the more you play, the more profound it gets. They say one's entire life can be experienced in a single round of Omok... \r\n#b(Join the Omok wait list by talking to Do Gong.)#k
